models.title: Models
models.about: One setup for the kit and all its projects. Providers first — API connections; then roles in each capability: a provider and a model, and with the «+» button, fallbacks in order.
models.load_failed: The model setup did not load
models.scope: Applies to every project on the machine ({n}); a project has no model setup of its own. File:
models.leftover: The .env of project «{name}» still has model variables — they no longer apply, remove them: {keys}
models.saved: Model setup saved — it applies to every project
models.ping_save_first: Save your changes first — the saved setup is what gets checked
models.providers_about: A provider is an API connection: address, key and how many requests it takes. A work gateway, a home llama.cpp, an embeddings service — each one its own provider. Models are picked in roles.
models.providers_empty: No providers yet. Add the first one — or create it right in a role while picking the model.
models.list_failed: The provider gave no model list — type the name by hand
models.p_drop_used: Provider «{name}» is used in roles ({n}). Delete it together with those backends?
models.key_set: key saved — type a new one to replace it
models.template_bad: not JSON — the field will not be saved
models.cap_about.llm: Roles of the language model. Engine roles are called by tasks: parsing and theses, planner, critic, answers. Each role has a primary backend and fallbacks in order: if the primary does not answer, the request goes to the next one.
models.cap_about.ocr: Scan recognition by a vision model. While the role has no backend, a scan honestly stays unparsed: a text model does not refuse an image, it makes things up. A fallback may be a different model.
models.cap_about.embeddings: Vectors for searching the base. A fallback is used only with the same model: another model's vectors live in another space, and swapping silently breaks search. No backend — search goes by words.
models.role_id_hint: The role's name for the engine and tasks
models.role_drop_ask: Delete role «{name}» together with its backends?
models.role_empty_engine: No backends — this role's tasks go to «{name}».
models.role_empty: No backends — pick a provider and a model.
models.thinking_hint: Faster without reasoning, but theses embellish and the critic goes blind (PRJ-A measurement 21.09.2026).
models.new_provider_about: A new provider — it will also appear in the «Providers» tab.
models.context_hint: How many tokens this model takes at this provider. Empty — not declared: the engine does not drop big requests in advance.
models.url_hint: If the embeddings or recognition service lives at another address than the provider's API.
models.enabled_hint: A switched-off backend stays in the chain, but no requests go to it.
models.other_space: another model — will not join the ring
models.other_space_hint: An embeddings fallback is used only with the same model as the primary.
models.run_about: Shared by all roles. «At once» is the run's cap: you can write «auto» — then the sum of provider widths is used; a number cuts it.
models.measure_hint: Growing batches of requests to each provider: how many it really takes at once. The result is in the console.
models.run_debug_hint: The agent run stops at the first error instead of going on through the cards. For finding a cause, not for work.
models.ping_failed: The check did not answer — the panel is unreachable or was interrupted.
models.role_empty_default.llm: No backends — the agent has nothing to run on: pick a provider and a model.
models.role_empty_default.ocr: No backends — scan recognition is off. Name the model explicitly: a guessed name gives not a refusal but a coherent fabrication.
models.role_empty_default.embeddings: No backends — semantic search is off.
models.role_about.worker: Writes: cards from sources, theses, the “Ask” answer, the “Productivity” document text, links in theses, aliases and transliteration.
models.role_about.planner: Plans: parsing a source and meetings, extracting foreign definitions, splitting long cards, the “Productivity” document plan (with tools and MCP).
models.role_about.critic: Checks decisions: parsed cards, the “empty” verdict, twins, Jira tasks, aliases, the golden set, the “Productivity” document.
models.role_about.qa: Momus: looks for unsupported claims in theses, “Ask” answers and documents; card clashes; automatic story review.
models.calls.about: Where the engine calls models: when, which roles by step, by which prompt and with which tools. Chains come from the setup on this page, including unsaved edits. The catalogue is matched against the code by the kit's tests.
models.calls.prompt_project: The prompt is a project file: {path}
models.calls.chosen_hint: The role or exactly a model is chosen where the call starts; here — the default role
models.calls.direct: A direct request to the gateway
models.calls.no_models: no models — the role is empty, and so is the default role
models.calls.via: (the role is empty — the “{name}” role works)
models.p_vpn_hint: A profile from the «Connection check» section: while it is down the kit does not call this provider and does not cycle through the ring blindly. «no VPN» — the provider does not depend on profiles.
models.p_health_hint.off: The availability of the profile is enough. Turn it on if the VPN is up but the provider is sometimes down.
models.p_health_hint.reach: The kit requests the endpoint and counts the provider alive on any answer except server errors.
models.p_health_hint.auth: The kit requests the endpoint with the provider's key and expects a successful answer. The key goes only to the provider's own address and only over https (or on this computer).
models.p_health_path_hint: A path on the provider's server. Example: /models
models.conflict: The model setup changed on disk since the page was opened. Your edits are still on the page: press «Discard changes» to load the fresh setup, then make them again.
models.broken_ask: The model setup file cannot be parsed (a hand edit?). Saving will replace it entirely; a copy stays beside it. Replace it?
models.slots_about: The primary of a role's chain gets tasks first; a provider has as many threads as its width (“Requests at once”), and the overall cap does not raise it.
models.help.p_id.what: The provider's internal name in the kit setup. Roles use it to know where to send requests.
models.help.p_id.how: gw1 — gateway №1 from the old setup; provider — a provider added with the “+ Provider” button.
models.help.p_id.result: The setup name does not change. How the provider is labelled on screen is set by the “Name” field.
models.help.used_in.what: How many roles on the LLM, OCR and Embeddings tabs take a model from this provider — as the primary or a fallback.
models.help.used_in.how: “used in roles: 6” — six roles send requests here.
models.help.used_in.result: 0 — the provider is set up but gets no work. Deleting the provider also removes it from these roles.
models.help.p_slots.what: How many threads of a parallel run start on this provider (the Writer role).
models.help.p_slots.how: “threads in a run: 24” — the provider has “Requests at once” = 24 and is the Writer's primary.
models.help.p_slots.result: The primary of the chain goes first; a fallback gets the call when the primary does not answer. The run-wide “At once” ceiling cuts the sum of all providers' threads.
models.help.list_n.what: How many models the provider returned for the “Ask for models” button.
models.help.list_n.how: “models: 12” — any of the twelve can be picked in roles.
models.help.list_n.result: The list is only for picking a model in roles and lives until the page reloads; it does not affect the engine.
models.help.p_name.result: This is how the provider is labelled in roles, the log and the “Threads” button hint. It does not affect the engine.
models.help.p_type.what: What server is behind the address.
models.help.p_type.how: OpenAI-compatible — the work gateway and most services; llama.cpp, vLLM, SGLang, Ollama — your own server; TEI — an embeddings service.
models.help.p_type.result: For now it is a label for people: the engine talks to any provider through the OpenAI-compatible API.
models.help.p_url.what: The provider's API address — with /v1 if the server needs it.
models.help.p_url.result: Requests of every role that picked this provider go here, and so does the “Ask for models” button.
models.help.p_key.what: The API access key (token). It is kept in the kit setup on this machine; the page does not show it.
models.help.p_key.how: The key the gateway owners gave you. Empty — a server without a key.
models.help.p_key.result: A wrong or expired key — the gateway answers 401/403, alarms show “key or access refused”, and there are no answers until the key is fixed.
models.help.p_vpn.what: Through which connection profile (VPN) the provider is reachable. Profiles are set up in the Connection check section.
models.help.p_vpn.how: Work gateway — the work VPN profile; a home model — “no VPN”.
models.help.p_vpn.result: While the profile is down, the kit does not call the provider and does not run requests around the ring blindly.
models.help.p_health.what: Whether to check the provider itself, not only the connection profile.
models.help.p_health.how: “answers with the key” — for a gateway that is sometimes down while the VPN is up.
models.help.p_health.result: A provider that fails the check counts as unreachable, as with a profile that is down. “do not check” — the profile being up is enough.
models.help.p_health_path.what: The path on the provider's server that the kit requests for the check.
models.help.p_health_path.result: A wrong path — the check fails, and the provider counts as unreachable.
models.help.p_width.what: How many requests this server takes at once — at least 1.
models.help.p_width.how: Work gateway — 24; a home llama.cpp with one slot — 1. Not sure — the “Measure gateways” button.
models.help.p_width.result: This many threads of a parallel run go to the provider; the run-wide “At once” ceiling does not raise them.
models.help.p_heavy.what: How many heavy requests (from the “Heavy from” threshold) to send this server at once. Empty — the engine learns the limit by itself after the first 529 refusal.
models.help.p_heavy.how: The gateway queues heavy requests two per worker and answers 529 beyond that — set 3.
models.help.p_heavy.result: Extra heavy requests wait for a place, short ones go at the full width. Lower — no 529 refusals, but heavy requests go slower. “Measure gateways” does not show this limit: it measures with short requests.
models.help.p_heavy_tokens.what: From what size a request counts as heavy. The size is the engine's estimate: the whole request including its cached part, three characters per token.
models.help.p_heavy_tokens.how: 32,768 — the default: from this many uncached tokens a gateway with a queue treats a request as expensive. If the gateway owners name their own number, enter it.
models.help.p_heavy_tokens.result: Lower — more requests fall under the “Heavy at once” limit, and work slows down. Higher — large requests go in a burst and may get 529. A 529 to a request below the threshold does not narrow heavy requests.
models.help.p_parallel.what: Whether the provider gets threads of a parallel run.
models.help.p_parallel.how: Clear it for a slow fallback — for example, a home model behind the work gateway.
models.help.p_parallel.result: A cleared provider gets no stream of tasks: it waits for its turn in the chain and answers when the primary did not.
models.help.p_template.what: Your own fields of the model's chat template (chat_template_kwargs) that the kit adds to every request to this provider. Format — JSON.
models.help.p_template.result: The fields go into the request as they are. “enable_thinking” has no effect here: whether the model reasons is decided by the role setting. Invalid JSON is not saved.
